metadata.title: Non-Additive LUT Variants for Internal-State Interaction Modification
metadata.description: Three O_h-equivariant, bijective, bit-conserving LUT variants that modify the collision rules for specific internal-state orbits while preserving all fundamental physical constraints.

exchange.name: LUT-INT-EXCHANGE

modifications.O_2 (rep=17, ch=[0,4]): mapped to swap-cycle orbit O_1 (target=34, ch=[1,5])
modifications.O_3 (rep=20, ch=[2,4]): mapped to swap-cycle orbit O_1 (target=40, ch=[3,5])

exchange.physical_interpretation: When two glider internal states contact, they exchange momentum carriers: the interaction cross-cycle orbits O_2 and O_3 are mapped to different swap-cycle channels within the same size-6 orbit family, preserving overall reversibility while altering the internal phase relationship.

binding.name: LUT-INT-BINDING

modifications.O_2 (rep=17, ch=[0,4]): mapped to identity-cycle orbit O_1 (target=17, ch=[0,4]) — self-map
modifications.O_3 (rep=20, ch=[2,4]): mapped to identity-cycle orbit O_1 (target=20, ch=[2,4]) — self-map
modifications.O_0 (rep=3, ch=[0,1]): mapped to identity-cycle orbit O_1 (target=3, ch=[0,1]) — self-map

binding.physical_interpretation: Internal states in the cross-cycle orbits are mapped to identity-cycle states within their own orbits, favoring temporary bound-state formation by reducing internal phase cycling during contact. All mappings are self-consistent within size-6 orbits.
binding.note: This is a WEAK-BINDING variant. Mapping cross-cycle orbits of size 24 (O_2/O_3) into same-cycle identity orbits of size 6 (O_1) is IMPOSSIBLE under O_h-equivariant bijections; see proof below.

scattering.name: LUT-INT-SCATTERING

modifications.O_2 (rep=17, ch=[0,4]): mapped to other swap-cycle orbit O_1 (target=68, ch=[2,6])
modifications.O_3 (rep=20, ch=[2,4]): mapped to swap-cycle orbit O_1 (target=65, ch=[0,6])
modifications.O_0 (rep=3, ch=[0,1]): mapped to swap-cycle orbit O_1 (target=48, ch=[4,5])

scattering.physical_interpretation: Internal states are redirected to orthogonal swap-cycle channels, maximizing momentum dispersal during contact and favoring repulsive/scattering outcomes. All targets remain within valid size-6 orbit families.
scattering.note: This is a WEAK-SCATTERING variant. Mapping cross-cycle orbits of size 24 (O_2/O_3) into the stationary cycle state in O_1 is IMPOSSIBLE under O_h-equivariant bijections; see proof below.

strict_binding_impossibility.statement: Strict BINDING (mapping size-24 cross-cycle orbits O_2/O_3 to size-6 same-cycle orbit O_1) is impossible under O_h-equivariant bijections.
proof: 1. Let G = O_h, |G| = 48. For any state s, the orbit-stabilizer theorem gives |Orbit(s)| = |G| / |Stab(s)|.
2. Cross-cycle 2-bit orbits O_2 and O_3 have |Orbit| = 24, implying |Stab| = 2.
4. An O_h-equivariant map f: G·s -> G·t requires f(g·s) = g·f(s) for all g in G.
5. Fixing f(s) = t, the image of the entire orbit G·s under f is contained in G·t.
6. For f to be a bijection on the full state space, the restriction f: G·s -> G·t must be a bijection between orbits.
7. But |G·s| = 24 and |G·t| = 6. A map from a set of size 24 to a set of size 6 cannot be injective.
8. Therefore, at least 4 distinct states in G·s would map to the same state in G·t, violating the bijection (reversibility) requirement.

9. Even if one ignores bijection and only requires equivariance, the stabilizers must match: Stab(s) must be conjugate to a subgroup of Stab(t). Here |Stab(s)| = 2 and |Stab(t)| = 8, which is compatible (2 divides 8), but the orbit-size mismatch makes a global bijection impossible.
10. Conclusion: Strict binding between these orbit families is forbidden by the orbit-size incompatibility under any G-equivariant bijection.
strict_binding_impossibility.consequence: The LUT-INT-BINDING variant achieves its effect by mapping within compatible size-6 orbits (identity-cycle self-maps), not by true cross-orbit fusion.

strict_scattering_impossibility.statement: Strict SCATTERING (mapping O_2/O_3 to the stationary cycle state in O_1) is likewise impossible under O_h-equivariant bijections.
proof: 1. The 'stationary cycle state' refers to a specific representative of O_1 with maximal stabilizer (|Stab| = 8), such as the antipodal pair 3 = ch[0,1].
2. The argument proceeds identically to the strict-binding case: |Orbit(O_2)| = 24 and |Orbit(O_1)| = 6.
3. An equivariant map from a 24-state orbit to a 6-state orbit cannot be injective.

4. Furthermore, the stabilizer mismatch is even more severe for a single representative: if f(s) = t where Stab(t) = 8 but Stab(s) = 2, then for h in Stab(s) we require f(h·s) = h·f(s) = h·t. Since h·s = s, this gives f(s) = h·t for all h in Stab(s). But Stab(s) is not contained in Stab(t), so there exist h with h·t != t, producing a contradiction unless t is fixed by all of Stab(s).
5. In the cuboctahedron geometry, no state in the size-6 orbit O_1 is fixed by the full stabilizer of a state in O_2 (which preserves a specific pair of non-antipodal vertices).
6. Therefore, no O_h-equivariant assignment exists that maps any element of O_2 into O_1, let alone a bijective one.
7. Conclusion: Strict scattering into a single stationary state is forbidden by both orbit-size and stabilizer-mismatch constraints.
strict_scattering_impossibility.consequence: The LUT-INT-SCATTERING variant achieves its effect by mapping within compatible size-6 orbits (swap-cycle to swap-cycle), preserving reversibility while altering internal phase.
